From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime API: sudden p99/p95 latency spike during morning traffic

Quick update from SRE: we observed a correlation between the latency spike and an automated prefix TTL-reset job that ran at 08:34:21 PT for a group of hosted partitions. The job triggered mass prefix invalidations on several KV shards, which caused a wave of cache-misses and synchronous backend reads — that aligns with the 12 minute window you reported.

What we have captured so far: attached kv-metrics and tail traces. Key observations:
- A TTL sweep performed a full prefix tombstone on ~12% of warmed prefix entries across the affected pool.
- When prefixes were re-requested, the runtime fell back to cold KV lookups and the request path incurred ~180-300ms additional latency on p99 requests.
- We did not deploy new model binaries or change kernel selection at the time.

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:28 PT:
- Rolled back the TTL-sweep config that caused aggressive invalidations.
- Enabled an emergency routing policy to route Nimbus tokens to a warm pool and throttle low-priority background jobs.
- Kicked an async prefix warmup for high-volume tokens.

Attachments: prefix_cache_warmup.log; kv-metrics-20260811.csv (samples and percentiles).

Next steps:
- Root cause: TTL-sweep logic used an incorrect shard selector when a batch job executed during high traffic; fix in progress and patch targeting 2026-08-12 14:00 PT for full roll-out.
- Follow-up: add safety guard to avoid mass invalidation during >=50% CPU utilization or >10k rps.

I'll post a postmortem draft to INF-3245 and share the impact table there.

— Marcus
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Realtime API: sudden p99/p95 latency spike during morning traffic

Sara — thanks again for flagging this and for your patience. Below is a short executive summary and what we've done to contain the issue.

Executive summary:
- What happened: An automated prefix TTL-reset sweep executed during high traffic and incorrectly selected a broad shard range, causing mass prefix invalidations and a temporary increase in p95/p99 latency.
- Impact: ~12 minutes of elevated tail latency starting at 08:34 PT on 2026-08-11. Approximately 6% of Realtime API requests for your tenant experienced timeouts during that window. No data corruption or message loss was observed.
- Mitigation: We rolled back the TTL-sweep config at 09:28 PT, rerouted your tokens to a warm pool, and kicked an async warmup job. We continue to monitor.

Proposed remediation and next steps:
- 10% service credit applied to the invoice for 2026-08 billing cycle (pending your confirmation).
- We will share a technical appendix (logs and traces) to your security contact and provide a postmortem within 48 hours (Jira INF-3245).
- Permanent fixes: add safety guards to sweep jobs, dry-run shard selector logic, and add realtime alerts on prefix invalidation spikes. ETA for patch: 2026-08-12 14:00 PT.

Technical appendix (high level): attached kv-metrics-20260811.csv and prefix_cache_warmup.log. If your team wants a call to walk through traces, I'm happy to schedule an SRE deep-dive.

Actions for Nimbus to consider: pinning a model variant to a dedicated warm pool during peak windows (we can help with configuration).

Would you like us to proceed with the 10% credit and schedule a technical call tomorrow?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
